claims.text: The as-processed (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The as-processed alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing will refine the grain structure of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The intervention can produce an ultrafine, recrystallized microstructure.
Severe plastic deformation creates a high density of defects and refines the grains.
Annealing temperature and duration control the extent of recrystallization after severe plastic deformation.
Ultrafine grain boundaries act as barriers to crack propagation.
The refined microstructure will inhibit crack initiation and propagation in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
Severe plastic deformation followed by annealing can improve the alloy's mechanical integrity and toughness.
The treated alloy will have greater compressive strength than the unchanged alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit improved resistance to cracking relative to the unchanged alloy.
Controlled annealing can recrystallize the alloy without altering the phases responsible for its caloric effects.
The caloric entropy change or field-induced temperature change will remain comparable to that of the unchanged alloy.
The intervention is applicable under the same magnetic-field, pressure-field, temperature, and mechanical-loading regimes used for the unchanged alloy.
Processing temperatures and deformation rates must be restricted so that the functional caloric phases are not altered.
The optimal strain, strain rate, annealing temperature, and annealing duration remain experimentally undetermined.
